title: Hallowe'en wedding sees Ayrshire couple tie the knot in haunted castle
excerpt: Ayrshire couple tie the knot at Dundonald Castle in a spooky Hallowe'en wedding, with pumpkins, fairy lights and smoke bombs
content:
IF you're going to get married at Hallowe'en, you might as well do it in real style...

That's exactly what Claire Thomson and partner Ryan Beckett did at the weekend - with a twilight wedding at Dundonald Castle.

The Irvine couple tied the knot surrounded by pumpkins and fairy lights, with a skeleton at the bottom of the hill directing guests to the castle.

(Image: Peter Stevenson)

Claire, 41, who runs the Wicked Kilwinning salon, said: "I have always had a fascination with Hallowe'en, its my absolute favourite time of year.

"It has always been a dream to get married on Hallowe'en, in a haunted castle."

(Image: Peter Stevenson)

Claire and Ryan, 37, described the big day as "absolutely brilliant".

The bride added: "Myself and Ryan have been together for almost four years. We're becoming a blended family - I have two kids, he has kids. Maisie is 21, Sam is 17, Kai is eight and Willow is five."

(Image: Peter Stevenson)

There were spooky songs while the guests arrived before the traditional hand tied ceremony at 4.30pm on Saturday, October 31, followed by sparklers and smoke bombs for the photos, then warm apple cider for the guests.

(Image: Peter Stevenson)

A party bus, fitted out with booze and smoke machines and karaoke, took the party to Kilwinning Bowling Club for the reception.

(Image: Peter Stevenson)

There, C&J party hire had transformed the venue into a spooky season extravaganza.

Claire said: "Craig and Julie did a fantastic job at the bowling club and turned it into a massive Hallowe'en party with indoor fireworks and dry ice.

"We made sure all our suppliers were local. I'm a business owner/hairdresser and I'm always grateful when people choose me."

(Image: Peter Stevenson)

A chippy van arrived to feed the guests, along with an ice cream van, while an artist from Valheim Tattoo in Saltcoats was there too, providing real tiny tattoos/Hallowe'en flash sheets for the guests.

(Image: Peter Stevenson)

Even the DJ dressed as the Grim Reaper - playing Michael Jackson's Thriller as the couple entered the room.

(Image: Peter Stevenson)

There was also a trick or treat table filled with lots of goodies from Black Moon Bakery in Troon.

The wedding venue, Dundonald Castle, is believed to be haunted by the ghost of Marjorie Bruce.

(Image: Peter Stevenson)

The daughter of King Robert the Bruce, she was thrown from her horse while heavily pregnant.

She died after giving birth to her son, the future King Robert II, who would later order the castle to be constructed as his home.

After the spectacular wedding bash, Claire said: "Were still on cloud nine. It was the most beautiful day."
